props.gloss_en: on the eighth day they returned to the lottery, as on the other festivals (the mishnah adds: one who offered bulls today does not offer tomorrow, but they rotate)
(entertained) the mishnah is Rebbi's and not the Rabbis'
Rebbi: for the bull that comes on the eighth day they cast lots from the start
the Sages: one of the two watches that did not offer bulls three times offers it
do the two [remaining] watches not need to cast lots [between them]? -- they do
the mishnah's lottery on the eighth day fits even the Rabbis
all the watches offer [bulls] twice and three times, except two watches that offer twice and not three times
(entertained) that baraita is Rebbi's and not the Rabbis' (for whom one of the two would offer a third bull on the eighth)
even per the Rabbis: 'did not offer three times' means in the bulls of the festival [of Sukkot]
one who offered bulls today does not offer [bulls] tomorrow; rather they rotate
R' Elazar: these seventy bulls -- to what do they correspond? to the seventy nations
why a single bull [on the eighth day]? it corresponds to the singular nation
a parable: a king of flesh and blood said to his servants, make me a great feast; on the last day he said to his beloved, make me a small feast so that I may enjoy [it] from you
R' Yochanan: woe to the nations, who lost and do not know what they lost
while the Temple stands the altar atones for them; and now, who atones for them?
